traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Dipterocarpaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate; leaves evergreen; stipules present; plants hermaphrodite; ovary usually superior, rarely half inferior; stems woody; flowers usually in panicles, sometimes in racemes, rarely in cymes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit usually nut, sometimes capsule; parts of each whorl 5; stamens (5-) 15 (-100); carpels 2 to 3 (-5). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
